newsitem.title: UK: Roaster buying helps LIFFE coffee off lows.
newsitem.headline: Roaster buying helps LIFFE coffee off lows.

text.p: LIFFE coffee prices fell in light trading, but bounced off support amid some industry price fixing at the lows, traders said.
"It's what we'd have expected," one trader said. "There was a lot of roaster buying keeping it off the lows.
The benchmark May contract last traded $11 lower at $1,718, having seen a low of $1,679. May volume was 2,726 lots of a total 3,735 lots.
A recovery in New York helped coffee to wipe out much of its losses in late trading.
In fundamental news, Ivorian commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze said on Monday the government had decided to destroy all coffee and cocoa planted illegally in national forests.
Speaking to reporters at the International Cocoa Organization talks, Gauze said that these illegal plantings had amounted to around 100,000 tonnes of cocoa and coffee last year.
"We will destroy all this anarchic production, with immediate effect," he said.
